name: two_bodies_do_not_export
why: THE RED OF THE CHECK, and it is the one that can be built with today's catalogue. Two bodies are not a defect -- a weldment has ten by construction -- but for a print they are: an STL of two bodies is two separate shells, and the printer does not know which of the two is the part. Each single body here is sound, and the judgement must be «no» all the same: if the count of the bodies were not there, this case would be green and the part wrong.
_why_the_raw_numbers_stay_healthy: Check(), Check2(), Check3 and Diagnose have nothing to object to on either of the two: that is exactly the point. The question «is it printable» is not the question «is it broken», and an operation that answers only the second passes this case.

expect._why_zero: the two bodies are sound: it is the judgement that says no, not the defects

does_not_include: as geometry it can be exported

steps._why_the_name: Entry Z-C16: the number of a body changes from one run to the next (measured on 25/9/2026 on this same part: the copy was C1 in one run out of three). The body is named by NAME, and the expectation «measurements.bodies[0].body = C1» -- which asked for the order, not the body -- is no longer there. The two bodies here are equal, and the check of only one has the same judgement: the case proves the road of the single body, not which of the two.

expect._why_one: asking for ONE body, the answer is about that one, and the count of the bodies of the part does not enter the judgement: on the single body the question is «is it sound», not «is it the whole part»
